forecaster_note: Mon: slow start to the week — a couple of waist-high peaky waves from the small swell mix; S-facing beaches hold the best shape. Clean in the morning with offshores and the low tide helping banks, then NE'lies send us running for cover in the arvo. Tue: mostly waist-high, pretty junky; cleanest in N corners out of the N/NE wind — morning low is the window. Fri: short-range S swell peaks overnight and fades, S-facing beaches well overhead early. — Surfline forecaster Max Stanley-Jones, Mon 2 Nov

wind.summary: Light N 4 kph at dawn, 7 kph by 9am; NE onshore 13 kph by noon, ENE 20 kph by 3pm. Light showers around.

shark.summary: Shark sighted by SLS drone at Whale Beach (Palm Beach→Manly zone) at 5:43pm Sun 1 Nov (~12.6h ago), water evacuated. No detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the last 24h (most recent nearby: tagged white shark #2895 at North Steyne, 10:28pm Wed 28 Oct). Feed current (newest statewide ~3h old); 40 real detections statewide in 24h. DPINSW returned 0 features. Absence of detections is not a guarantee — check the live map before paddling out.

days.note: 192 kJ (123 from a 9s dead-S, 67 from a 7s NE wind wave) — small, peaky waist-high; S-facing banks best. Clean light N at dawn, NE onshore from noon: surf 6–9:30am around the 8:26am low.
days.surfline_text: Bit of a slow start to the week as we'll only see a couple waist high waves from the small swell mix - peaky. S facing beaches will probably hold the best shape. Clean in the morning with offshores and that low tide will help banks out - then NE'lies will send us running for cover in the arvy.
